title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the basic theory of divided powers (PD structures) as foundations for crystalline cohomology. Axioms 1.1–1.6 on the previous pages are the usual PD axioms, phrased for a 'pseudo-ring' (a non-unital algebra, i.e. an ideal regarded abstractly) over a base ring Λ (or A). 1.6 is π^n(λx)=λ^nπ^n(x), which holds automatically when the base is Z.

§2 (end). For an A-module M he takes the divided power algebra Γ(M)=⊕Γ^n(M). He extends the maps x↦x^{(n)} from M to all of Γ^+(M)=⊕_{n≥1}Γ^n(M). On Γ^p(M) this is done through the homogeneous polynomial law of degree np given by x↦x^{(pn)}·(pn)!/((p!)^n n!). This page asserts that these π^n satisfy 1.1–1.6. So Γ^+(M), viewed as an ideal of Γ(M), becomes a PD algebra. The canonical linear map M→Γ^+(M) is universal among linear maps from M into PD algebras, i.e. Γ is left adjoint to the forgetful functor from PD algebras to modules. This is Roby's theorem.

§3. Given a ring A and an ideal I, he looks for the universal ring map u:A→B with (B,J,γ) a PD ring and u(I)⊂J, i.e. the PD envelope D_A(I). His first presentation is the A-algebra generated by symbols π^n x (n≥2, x in the ideal) subject to relations 1.2–1.6, with π^1(x) read as x. His second presentation, continued on the next page, goes as follows:
- form Γ^+_A(I);
- quotient by the PD ideal generated by (x·y)^{(n)} − x^n * y^{(n)}, which yields a PD algebra I';
- take the extension A ×_I I', i.e. (A ⊕ I')/{(x,−x')}.

This is the standard construction of the PD envelope found in Berthelot's thesis (1974), Berthelot–Ogus, and the Stacks Project.
errors: Notational slip: §3 starts with an ideal I of A, but the generators π^n x are then taken with x∈J. Here J should be I, the ideal of A; J was the PD ideal of B. The next page continues with J for the ideal of A.
The page only asserts ('on vérifie') that the extended π^n satisfy 1.1–1.6. The verification is nontrivial (Roby), especially for the composition axiom π^m∘π^n. No gap beyond omission.
In the first presentation, the relations for x∈I must also include the identification of π^1(x) with the image of x∈A, and compatibility with the ring structure of A. These are only partly stated.

ideas.what: PD structure on Γ^+_A(M) extending x↦x^{[n]}, and universality of M→Γ^+(M) among linear maps to PD algebras
ideas.modern_name: Divided power algebra Γ_A(M) as free PD algebra on M
ideas.where_published: Roby, Ann. ENS 1963 / C. R. 1965; Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407), ch. I

ideas.what: Universal PD thickening of (A,I): ring map A→B sending I into a PD ideal J
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (thesis, LNM 407, 1974); idea in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1966/68)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', in Dix exposés (1968), mentions PD envelopes; details in Berthelot LNM 407

ideas.what: Construction of the envelope as a quotient of Γ^+_A(I) by relations (xy)^{[n]}=x^n y^{[n]}, followed by gluing with A
ideas.modern_name: Standard presentation of the PD envelope (Stacks Project, Berthelot–Ogus §3)
ideas.where_published: Berthelot LNM 407; Berthelot–Ogus 'Notes on crystalline cohomology' (1978)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard foundational material: Roby's PD structure on Γ^+(M) and the PD envelope construction later written up by Berthelot. Historically mildly interesting as Grothendieck's own early sketch of the envelope construction, but nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ^*(A,J)' — the ideal should be I; the symbol looks like Γ^* (or Γ^+). Content: the A-algèbre Γ(A,I).
'et comme pour un tel [?] universel' — likely 'et est pour cela universel' or similar, i.e. the map M→Γ^+(M) is universal; reading uncertain.
The base ring is written Λ in the first lines ('Λ-algèbre', 'Λ-modules'), consistent with the N.B. on the next page about a base ring Λ.
